name: Gene Amdahl
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: computerhistory.org/profile/gene-myron-amdahl/ names him a 1998 Computer History Museum Fellow, citation "For his fundamental work in computer architecture and design, project management, and leadership" -- an enumerated annual honour list naming the person, not a feature article. a1: born 16 November 1922 (Wikipedia). a2: PhD in theoretical physics, University of Wisconsin-Madison, 1952 -- the last credential completed, after a 1948 BS in engineering physics from South Dakota State; his PhD work was the WISC computer, so the doctorate and the domain entry are the same event. a3: joined IBM June 1952, immediately after the PhD (Wikipedia). a4: Amdahl Corporation incorporated 19 October 1970 (International Directory of Company Histories text carried by fundinguniverse and company-histories.com). SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK: Amdahl Corporation is his FIRST venture and also the famous one -- Trilogy Systems (1979), Andor International (1987) and Commercial Data Servers (1996) are all later, and everything before 1970 was salaried employment (IBM 1952-56 and 1960-69; Ramo-Wooldridge/Aeronutronic in between). No earlier venture found. a5 rev10 = 1975, against the 1975 nominal bar of $1,671,103 (python -m src.cpi 1975), NOT $10M nominal. The company was pre-revenue for its first four and a half years: it shipped no product until the first Amdahl 470 V/6 went to NASA Goddard in June 1975, so no earlier crossing is possible and the founding year is not needed as a bound. The IDCH company history states revenues "climbed from less than $14 million in 1975 to $321 million in 1977", and the unit price of a 470 V/6 was $3.5 million (ed-thelen.org/comp-hist/amdahl-bio-core-1-4.html, quoting the Core magazine biography: "the price was the same at $3.5 million"). Even the most conservative possible reading -- a single machine recognised in 1975 -- is $3,500,000, or 209% of that year's bar; the IDCH figure implies roughly 4x to 8x it. Margin is large under either reading. FALLBACK NOT USED and would have been barred: the 1976 IPO is a year later than the documented first-revenue year, and frame.md bars the fallback whenever an earlier crossing is known. a6: 1976, the year Amdahl Corporation went public, following the dataset's convention of using the later listing/liquidity event as the scale marker; the IDCH history records that the offering let the company convert debt to equity and turn profitable, and revenue reached $321 million with $48.2 million net income by 1977.

name: Konrad Zuse
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: computerhistory.org/profile/konrad-zuse/ names him a 1999 Computer History Museum Fellow (roster URL re-confirmed), citation "For his invention of the first program-controlled, electromechanical, digital computer and the first high-level programming language, 'Plankalkuel'". a1: born 22 June 1910 (Neue Deutsche Biographie via deutsche-biographie.de; de.wikipedia agrees). a2: Diplom in Bauingenieurwesen, TH Berlin-Charlottenburg, July 1935 -- the last and only credential completed (Abitur 1928). a3: July 1935, structural engineer at Henschel Flugzeug-Werke, Berlin-Schoenefeld, his first paid engineering post and the calculation drudgery that produced the machines; his first paid work on computing hardware specifically was the Henschel S1 special-purpose computer from about 1940, also as a Henschel employee, hence conf medium on the choice of 1935. SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK -- MATERIAL: Zuse KG (1949) is NOT his first venture. He set up "Dipl.-Ing. K. Zuse Ingenieurbuero und Apparatebau" in Berlin (NDB dates the name to May 1936, formally constituted April 1941; de.wikipedia gives 1941), and after the war a short-lived "Zuse-Ingenieurbuero, Hopferau" with Harro Stucken in autumn 1946. Neither can have been the crossing: the Berlin firm never exceeded about 20 staff, worked on individual development contracts (Henschel S1/S2, the Z4) rather than a product line, published no revenue, and was destroyed in 1945; the 1941 nominal rev10 bar was $456,603, about 1.14M Reichsmark at the official 2.50 RM/USD parity, which a 20-person Berlin workshop is not documented anywhere as approaching, and the Hopferau office was a two-man consultancy. No source documents a crossing by either, so the hit entity is Zuse KG, founded 1 August 1949 in Neukirchen (Kreis Huenfeld) with five to eight employees. a4 is recorded as 1941 (the formally constituted Berlin firm) rather than 1949, since the earlier venture is what a4 asks for; 1936 is the alternative reading and is why conf is medium. a5 rev10 = BOUNDED 1954-1961, a 7-year span, both ends sourced, against the constant-2026-dollar bar for each year, NOT $10M nominal. CURRENCY: DM/USD from the de.wikipedia Deutsche Mark rate table -- the Bretton Woods parity 4.20 DM/USD held from 1949 (table entry "1950/52: 4,2") to the March 1961 revaluation, and the table gives 4,0221 DM/USD for 1961. LOWER END, below the bar: the Neue Deutsche Biographie states of the early Zuse KG that Konrad Zuse "der Umsatz 1954 bis auf 1,3 Mio. DM anwachsen liess" -- 1954 turnover DM 1,300,000. The 1954 nominal rev10 bar is $835,552 (python -m src.cpi 1954), which at 4.20 DM/USD is DM 3,509,318, so 1954 revenue was 37% of the bar, clearly below. UPPER END, above the bar: the same NDB entry records that by 1961 turnover had reached about DM 9 million with more than 300 employees. The 1961 nominal bar is $928,736, or DM 3,735,466 at 4,0221 DM/USD, so DM 9,000,000 is 241% of the bar -- above by a wide margin, and above even on the pre-revaluation 4.20 rate (231%). The crossing therefore happened between 1954 and 1961; the intervening years are exactly the Z11 (from 1955, series production) and Z22 (from 1958, 55 units at about DM 250,000 each) ramp, and no source pins the single year. Neither end is a qualitative claim: both are DM figures from the NDB. FALLBACK NOT AVAILABLE AND NOT NEEDED: Zuse KG never listed; control passed to Rheinstahl/Brown Boveri in 1964 and to Siemens in 1967, both after the crossing, and no purchase price is published for either. a6: 1964, when Brown, Boveri & Cie took complete control after Zuse KG's financial difficulties, the company then standing at 1,200 employees and an order book above DM 25 million -- the later, larger-scale event, following this dataset's convention of a listing or change-of-control as the scale marker.

name: Thomas Frist Jr.
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: forbes.com/profile/thomas-frist-jr/ (the roster URL, re-fetched) shows "Thomas Frist, Jr. & family", "#65 in the world today", real-time net worth $34.2B as of 8/22/26, with a Self-Made Score of 7 -- inside the frame's self-made band of 6-10. The roster's cited rank of 48 is the published Billionaires 2026 list position; 65 is the live figure on the same profile page. a1: born 12 August 1938 (Wikipedia). a2: MD, Washington University School of Medicine, 1965 -- the last credential actually COMPLETED. He returned to Vanderbilt for a surgical residency but it was interrupted by two years as a US Air Force flight surgeon at Robins AFB and he left for HCA in 1968 without finishing it, so the residency is not the anchor (wustl commencement archive: "Dr. Frist, who earned his doctor of medicine degree from Washington University School of Medicine in 1965"; BA Vanderbilt 1961). a3: 1965, the start of his surgical residency and then Air Force flight-surgeon service -- his first paid work in the healthcare domain, immediately on the MD; conf medium because the exact start month of the residency is not published. SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK: HCA (1968) is his FIRST venture. Everything before it was training or military service; his other ventures -- China Health Care Corporation (2008) and Tomco II LLC -- are forty years later. His father's Park View Hospital (1960, Nashville) is NOT an earlier venture of his: Frist Jr. was an undergraduate and then a medical student when it was built, and it was contributed into HCA at formation. No earlier venture found. a5 rev10 = 1968, HCA's founding year, against the 1968 nominal bar of $1,080,937 (python -m src.cpi 1968), NOT $10M nominal. The International Directory of Company Histories text on encyclopedia.com states "Revenues in 1968 totaling $29 million and increasing to more than $1 billion in 1980." $29,000,000 is 2,683% of the 1968 bar -- the largest margin in this batch, and no earlier crossing is possible because the company did not exist before 1968. This is a dollar figure, not a qualitative scale claim. FALLBACK BARRED AND NOT NEEDED: the March 1969 NYSE IPO is a year after the documented crossing, exactly the defect frame.md warns about. a6: March 1969, HCA's NYSE listing, when the stock rose from $18 to $40 on the first day and the company operated 11 hospitals -- the later scale event.

name: Chung Yong-ji
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED with a caveat on the rank: forbes.com/profile/chung-yong-ji/ (the roster URL, re-fetched 22 Aug 2026) names him on The World's Billionaires, source of wealth "Self Made", and describes him as the 2001 founder of Caregen. RANK DISCREPANCY: the live profile shows #2856 with a $1.4B net worth, not the rank 268 the roster note cites for Billionaires 2026; membership and self-made status are confirmed, the roster's rank figure is not, and the mismatch is large enough to record. a1: born February 1970 (Business Post [Who Is ?] profile). a2: PhD in molecular biology, Cornell University, 2000 -- the last credential COMPLETED. The 2001 postdoctoral year at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine is training, not a credential, so it is not the anchor; earlier credentials are a 1994 BSc in genetic engineering from Sungkyunkwan University and a 1996 MSc in biochemistry from the University of Texas at San Antonio. a3: 2001, the Northwestern postdoctoral research post -- his first paid position in the domain; conf medium because it ran in the same year he founded the company and the sources give no months. SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK: Caregen, incorporated 17 August 2001, is his FIRST venture. His whole prior career was study and academic research (SKKU, UT San Antonio, Cornell, Northwestern) and the Business Post profile lists no company before Caregen. No earlier venture found. a5 rev10 = BOUNDED 2001-2011, a 10-year span, the widest frame.md permits, both ends sourced. LOWER END: the founding year, 17 August 2001 -- the company could not earn before it existed, which frame.md accepts as a valid lower bound. UPPER END: Caregen's own dated corporate history (caregen.co.kr/history) records the export-tower awards it received at Korea's Trade Day, a government/KITA award scale denominated in US dollars: 2007 one-million-dollar tower, 2008 three-million, 2010 five-million, 2011 TEN-MILLION-DOLLAR tower, 2015 thirty-million. The ten-million-dollar tower in 2011 certifies at least US$10,000,000 of exports in the qualifying year, and total revenue is at least exports, so 2011 revenue was at least $10,000,000 against the 2011 nominal rev10 bar of $6,986,920 (python -m src.cpi 2011) -- 143% of the bar, a 43% margin. NO CURRENCY CONVERSION IS NEEDED: the export-tower tiers are denominated in US dollars, so the KRW/USD rate never enters. CAVEAT ON THE UPPER-END SOURCE: this is the company's own history page recording a third-party government award rather than an independent report of it; two searches for independent Korean coverage of Caregen's 2011 ten-million-dollar tower returned nothing, hence conf medium. The rising tower tiers 2007-2011 are internally consistent with the crossing falling late in the range rather than early. FALLBACK BARRED: the 17 November 2015 Kosdaq listing is four years after a known crossing, and frame.md forbids dating the row by it. Post-listing financials (2023 revenue KRW 79.2bn, 2024 KRW 82.6bn, per Business Post) are far too late to date the crossing and were not used. a6: 17 November 2015, the Kosdaq listing.

name: Alyson Friedensohn
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster URL fortune.com/ranking/40-under-40/2019/alyson-friedensohn-and-erica-johnson/ re-fetched and it names her -- "Alyson Friedensohn and Erica Johnson", age 29 and 32, Industry: Health, company Modern Health, on Fortune's 2019 40 Under 40. Taken without her joint-entry co-founder Johnson, as the assignment directs. a1: BOUNDED 1989-1990. Fortune's 2019 list gives her age as 29, which places the birth in one of those two calendar years; no source gives a birth date, so this is bounded rather than pinned. Corroborated by her Forbes 30 Under 30 listing of December 2019, whose age cut-off is consistent. a2: UNKNOWN after four attempts. Her Forbes Councils profile states she "graduated with honors from Johns Hopkins University with a degree in Global Environmental Change and Sustainability" and the Forbes billionaire-tracker profile gives "Bachelor of Arts/Science, The Johns Hopkins University", but NO source anywhere gives a graduation year; the LinkedIn profile is behind a sign-in wall and the Y Combinator company page carries no founder bio. Recording unknown rather than deriving a year from her age is the honest outcome and is what the brief requires. a3: UNKNOWN. Her pre-founding career per the Forbes Councils profile ran PwC strategy consulting, then Keas (healthy behaviour change management, later acquired by Welltok), then Collective Health -- Keas being the first healthcare-domain role -- but no source dates any of them, so the anchor cannot be recorded. SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK: Modern Health is her FIRST venture. Every prior role (PwC, Keas, Collective Health, and CorePower Yoga instruction) is salaried employment, and no source names an earlier company. No earlier venture found. a4: 2017, the founding year given by Y Combinator's own company page ("Founded: 2017", batch Winter 2018) and by Contrary Research ("Founding Date Jan 2017"). EXCLUDED, crossing_undatable. Modern Health has never published a revenue or ARR figure and there is no fallback available: it has never listed and has never been acquired, so ipo and acq50 do not exist for this row. Everything that survives two rounds of checking is either a growth multiple with no base or a model estimate: the company's December 2020 Series C release says revenue "grew 25 times" since the Series B and that it served "190+ enterprises... most with more than 1,000 employees"; the April 2021 release gives "220+ enterprises globally" and a doubled customer base but no dollars; the September 2021 Series D put the valuation at $1.17B, and a valuation is not revenue; Contrary Research's 13-minute March 2023 company memo contains no revenue figure at all; Latka's $174.6M "ARR" for September 2024 is explicitly labelled on its own page as an estimate from "public sources and proprietary models" with no company interview behind it, which is exactly the weak source the brief says not to accept in order to dodge an exclusion; and the 2024 Inc. 5000 listing certifies only four-year growth of 600% and Inc.'s $2M minimum for the base year, both below the relevant bars. A BOUND WAS ATTEMPTED AND FAILS ON THE UPPER END, NOT THE LOWER: the founding year 2017 is a perfectly good lower bound, but frame.md requires the later end to be a source showing the venture at or above the bar in a stated year, and no such figure exists in any year. The bars checked were $8,039,032 for 2020 and $8,416,707 for 2021 (python -m src.cpi), constant-2026-dollar figures, not $10M nominal. Dating this row by the February 2021 unicorn round would be inventing a revenue event out of a financing, which this study does not do (same treatment as p145 Raycho Raychev). a6: UNKNOWN for the same reason -- Modern Health's later scale events are all private financings, and a funding round is not one of this study's a6 event types.
